q: Can I import my IdentityIQ XML objects (rules, applications, workflows) into Identity Security Cloud?
must: no direct import: ISC does not read IIQ XML; objects are rebuilt (UI, API, sp-config for supported ISC objects)
it is a re-architecture best done in phases with IIQ and ISC side by side; SailPoint offers an upgrade program/assessment (and AI-assisted tooling)
clean up unused applications, rules and custom objects first
must_not: says sp-config imports IIQ export files
source: Developer Community migration threads; SailPoint upgrade program
A: No. ISC does not import IIQ XML: every object is rebuilt in ISC (UI, REST API, or sp-config JSON for supported object types). Treat it as a re-architecture done in phases with IIQ and ISC side by side. Export the IIQ XML anyway as input for analysis (`python3 scripts/analyze_iiq.py iiq-export/ --plan migration-plan.md`), which classifies each object as direct/adapt/none and names the ISC equivalent. Rough mapping: Application -> Source + connector/schema/correlation config/Create Account; Rule -> transform, cloud rule (reviewed by SailPoint), connector rule (`POST /connector-rules/v1`) or configuration; Workflow -> ISC Workflows (no BeanShell; triggers/actions) plus access request config. Rules you keep must be rewritten without `context`, rule libraries, JDBC/HTTP, and pass review. SailPoint offers an Upgrade Assessment and, since June 2026, SailPoint Agentic Acceleration with an AI tool (Virtual Architect) that converts IIQ config, workflows and policies into an ISC starting point via its forward deployed engineers - still a starting point, not an import.
B: No. There is no import path for IIQ XML into ISC; the object models differ (no Application, Workflow, TaskDefinition, Rule-runner objects in ISC). Migration is a re-implementation: sources are recreated with ISC connectors (via UI or /v3/sources API, often using SaaS or VA-based connectors), applications/schemas reconfigured, correlation and attribute mappings rebuilt in identity profiles with transforms. Rules must be reviewed: many become transforms or out-of-box configuration; remaining BeanShell is rewritten into supported cloud rule types (submitted to SailPoint) or connector rules (deployed by you via the connector-rules API). IIQ workflows map to ISC Workflows (JSON, built in the visual editor, triggered by event triggers) or external services via event triggers. Use SailPoint's migration tooling/assessment (IIQ to ISC migration assessment) to inventory. Config can then be moved between ISC tenants using SP-Config (sp-config import/export) - but that's ISC-to-ISC only.

q: What happens to my IIQ AfterProvisioning rule that opens a ServiceNow ticket after an AD account is disabled?
must: ISC has no AfterProvisioning rule type
use a workflow triggered by the Provisioning Completed event (e.g. HTTP Request action or ServiceNow integration)
HTTP calls from cloud rules are not allowed anyway
must_not: says to convert it to an AfterProvisioning cloud rule
source: ISC supported cloud rules list; event triggers
A: ISC has no AfterProvisioning rule type, so it becomes an ISC Workflow (level: adapt). Trigger: Provisioning Completed (`idn:post-provisioning`, fire-and-forget), whose payload contains `accountRequests[]` with `source`, `accountId`, `accountOperation`, `provisioningResult`, plus `recipient`, `errors`. Add a filter/Compare step so it runs only when the source is your AD source, `accountOperation` is Disable and the result succeeded. Then create the ticket with the HTTP Request action (`sp:http`) against the ServiceNow Table API (OAuth/basic credentials in the action), or the ServiceNow action (`sp:snow`) if available in your tenant. Optional: Get Identity (`sp:get-identity`) for more context, Send Email (`sp:send-email`) on failure. Do not port the BeanShell: workflows don't run scripts, and any IIQ `context`/HTTP code is not allowed in cloud rules either. Alternatively subscribe an external service to the same event trigger. Test with the workflow test payload before enabling.
B: AfterProvisioning rules don't exist as a cloud rule type in ISC. Rebuild it as event-driven: subscribe to the 'Provisioning Completed' event trigger (idn:post-provisioning) and implement either an ISC Workflow (trigger: Provisioning Completed, filter for source = AD and operation Disable/accountRequests with op 'Disable', then an HTTP Request action calling the ServiceNow Table API or using the ServiceNow integration) or an external HTTP subscriber (e.g., a small serverless function). Use a JSONPath trigger filter like $.accountRequests[?(@.source.name == 'Active Directory' && @.accountOperation == 'Disable')] to reduce noise. Store ServiceNow credentials securely (workflow HTTP action auth / secrets). Alternatively, use SailPoint's ServiceNow Service Desk integration or Card connector. The AD connector-side AfterModify/AfterDisable native PowerShell rules exist on the IQService, but they're for target-side actions, not ticketing.

q: Our IIQ HR application has a Correlation rule, a Creation rule and a ResourceObjectCustomization rule. What do they become in ISC?
must: Correlation: use the source correlation config (attribute pairs) first; only if impossible a Correlation cloud rule returning identityAttributeName/identityAttributeValue without context
Creation: no creation rule; identity profile attribute mappings with transforms
Customization: no customization rule; transforms where values are used (BuildMap for file/JDBC, connector customizer for SaaS)
must_not: says all three can be submitted as ISC cloud rules unchanged
source: ISC cloud rules list; isc-sources correlation; transforms
A: All three are 'adapt'. Correlation rule -> the source's correlation configuration (attribute pairs, Equals, first match wins); only if that cannot express it, a Correlation cloud rule returning a Map with `identityAttributeName`/`identityAttributeValue` (needs SailPoint review). Creation (IdentityCreation) rule -> no ISC equivalent rule: use the HR source's identity profile attribute mappings with transforms (attributes are recomputed on every refresh, so logic must be idempotent; lifecycle state via a transform or IdentityAttribute rule). ResourceObjectCustomization -> no customization rule in ISC: apply transforms where the value is consumed (identity profile mappings); for Delimited File/JDBC sources use a BuildMap/JDBCBuildMap connector rule (runs on the VA, no `context`); for SaaS connectors a connector customizer. Prefer configuration and transforms first: transforms need no SailPoint review, while every cloud rule costs Expert Services review time. Build order: source, correlation, first aggregation, compare identities with IIQ, then identity profile/transforms, then lifecycle states.
B: Correlation rule: in ISC correlation for authoritative sources is configured in the source's Correlation config (attribute pairs, e.g., identity employeeNumber = account EMPLOYEE_ID); a cloud Correlation rule type exists if logic is too complex, but prefer config. Creation rule (IdentityCreation in IIQ): replaced by the Identity Profile attribute mappings using transforms; complex logic can use an IdentityAttribute rule (cloud rule) referenced from a transform of type 'rule'. Initial lifecycle state, manager etc. are also identity profile mappings (cloudLifecycleState via a transform). ResourceObjectCustomization: becomes a cloud ResourceObjectCustomization? In ISC this exists as a connector rule type 'ResourceObjectCustomization' for VA-based connectors; often replaced by transforms on the identity profile or by BuildMap/JDBCBuildMap (connector rules) for delimited/JDBC sources. Prefer transforms when the change is only for identity attributes.

q: We use IIQ QuickLinks, custom objects and a couple of plugins. What are the ISC options?
must: none of the three exist in ISC
QuickLinks: Request Center for access, Forms plus workflows (external trigger) for custom actions
custom objects: transform lookup tables/attributes or an external store; plugins: external apps using the ISC APIs (UI Development Kit)
must_not: says custom objects can be migrated to ISC as-is
source: Developer Community threads on custom objects and plugins
A: QuickLinks: ISC has no QuickLinks/custom forms framework like IIQ. Replace with Access Requests (request center), Forms (ISC Forms attached to workflows, Custom Forms), and Workflows with 'Form' actions or launchers (Workflow 'External Trigger' / 'Launchers' let users start workflows from the UI). Custom objects: no Custom object type; store config in source attributes, identity attributes, governance groups, transforms lookups (lookup transform tables), or external storage; workflows can call external APIs. Plugins: no plugin framework in ISC. Re-implement UI functionality as external apps using the ISC APIs (v3/beta) with PATs/OAuth clients, SaaS connectivity custom connectors (SaaS Connector SDK) for integration, event triggers for reactive logic, and the UI Development Kit (UI Dev Kit) for custom portals. Reports: use Search, saved searches/scheduled searches, and Data Access/Access Intelligence or export via APIs.
B: All three have no ISC equivalent (level: none) and need redesign. QuickLinks -> Request Center for access requests; for custom self-service actions, ISC Forms plus a Workflow (external trigger or Form submitted). Custom objects (sailpoint.object.Custom) -> lookup tables in transforms (`lookup` transform) for mapping data, identity/source attributes, or an external store you call from workflows (HTTP Request). Plugins -> an external application on the ISC APIs (SailPoint UI Development Kit), or workflows/event triggers for background logic. Also related: custom task executors and Run Rule tasks become scheduled workflows or external jobs on the ISC API. Rule libraries don't exist either (inline code). Inventory these early because they are typically the largest redesign items; retire unused ones during the IIQ cleanup step before migrating.

q: How do IIQ business roles with an IdentitySelector rule and IIQ CertificationExclusion rules migrate?
must: IdentitySelector rules are deprecated in ISC: use role membership (standard assignment) criteria
CertificationExclusion rules are deprecated: use campaign filters
business roles become ISC roles (containing access profiles/entitlements); IT roles usually access profiles
must_not: says to submit them as ISC cloud rules
source: rules index Deprecated Rules; roles/access profiles
A: Business roles with an IdentitySelector rule: ISC roles use membership criteria (Standard criteria on identity attributes, account attributes, entitlements with AND/OR up to limited nesting) or identity list. Translate the rule logic into criteria; if impossible, compute a derived identity attribute (via transform or IdentityAttribute rule) e.g. 'roleEligibility_X' and use it in the role criteria. Role-required access maps to the role's access profiles (entitlements bundled per source). IT roles/bundles don't map 1:1: IIQ IT roles become Access Profiles. CertificationExclusion rules: ISC has no such rule. Use certification campaign filters (campaign filter with inclusion/exclusion criteria on identity attributes, access, sources), campaign scope (search-based campaigns using query exclusions), and identity attribute based filters, plus 'Exclude' options in Manager/Source campaigns. Machine/service accounts can be excluded via filters on identity type or by not correlating them.
B: Both IIQ rule types are deprecated in ISC (the reviewer rejects them, check R005), so replace them with configuration. Business roles (Bundle type business) with an IdentitySelector rule -> ISC roles with membership criteria (identity attributes, account attributes, entitlements, combined with AND/OR) - level adapt; required/permitted roles and role inheritance must be flattened, and IT roles become access profiles (single source) or role access. If the selector logic can't be expressed, derive a helper identity attribute (transform) and base criteria on it. CertificationExclusion rules -> campaign filters on the ISC campaign (manager, source owner, search, role composition, machine account campaigns), excluding identities/access by attributes, sources, entitlements; certifier rules -> campaign reviewer type. Build roles in phase 5 (after sources and identity profiles) and campaigns last, after SOD policies.

q: What exactly do I need to send SailPoint to get a cloud rule reviewed, and how should the file be named?
must: support portal request (or support email) with the rule file, validator output, tenant name and approval for Expert Services hours
file named 'Rule - {type} - {name}.xml' matching the Rule type and name attributes
review is an integrity check against guidelines, not a check that the rule works; ~24h SLA weekdays
must_not: says rules are uploaded directly via API by the customer and need no review
says SailPoint tests the rule's logic
A: Open a request on the SailPoint support portal (or email support); reviews need an Expert Services contract (billable, typically 15-30 min per rule). Attach: (1) the rule XML (SailPoint template: XML declaration + sailpoint.dtd DOCTYPE, <Rule name=... type=...>, <Description>, code in CDATA, UTF-8) named exactly `Rule - {type} - {name}.xml`, e.g. `Rule - IdentityAttribute - Calculate Lifecycle.xml`; (2) validator output (e.g. `review_rule.py file.xml --report review.md`, plus SailPoint's community rule validator if used); (3) the tenant name (`acme-sb.identitynow.com` sandbox or `acme.identitynow.com` production); (4) approval for Expert Services to proceed. One rule per ticket unless rules must be deployed together. SLA: 24h for weekday submissions, next business day for weekends; ask 48h ahead for a specific deployment window. The review is an integrity check against guidelines, not a functional test, so test first (RDK/sandbox). Connector rules are different: created via `POST /connector-rules/v1` (JSON with escaped script and `signature`).
B: Open a ticket with SailPoint (Expert Services/support portal) requesting a cloud rule review/deployment for your tenant (give the org name/tenant URL). Attach the rule as a standalone SailPoint Rule XML file (with DOCTYPE sailpoint.dtd, <Rule name="..." type="...">, <Description>, optional <Signature> and the BeanShell inside <Source> wrapped in CDATA). Use one rule per file and name the file after the rule type and rule name, e.g. Rule - AttributeGenerator - Generate Unique Email.xml (convention: 'Rule - <Type> - <Name>.xml'); the name attribute in the XML should match. Prefix rule names consistently with your company/project. Include a short description of the purpose, which source/transform/identity profile it will be attached to, and whether it's new or an update (for an update, reference the existing rule name/ID so it is replaced, not duplicated). Make sure it compiles and was tested locally (e.g., with the rule validator tool) before submitting; SailPoint usually turns reviews around in a few business days. Connector rules (BeforeProvisioning on VA etc.) can instead be uploaded yourself via the /beta/connector-rules API after passing the validator.

q: My IdentityAttribute rule uses context.getObjectByName(Identity.class, managerId) to read the manager's email. Will it pass review? What should I use?
must: no: context and .getObjectByName() are on SailPoint's code-restriction list; new rules using them are returned
use IdnRuleUtil helpers via idn, e.g. idn.getIdentityById(id) or idn.findIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute(attr, "Equals", value, sortAttr)
consider a transform (e.g. reference/manager attribute) instead of a rule
must_not: says context is allowed read-only in cloud rules
A: No. `context.` and `.getObjectByName()` are both on SailPoint's code-restriction list (blocked by the platform, reviewer checks R020/R021): there is no IIQ `context` in ISC. An IdentityAttribute rule receives only `log`, `idn` (IdnRuleUtil, read-only), `identity` and `oldValue`, and must return `attributeValue`. Use IdnRuleUtil: if you have the manager's ID, `idn.getIdentityById(managerId)` (returns `sailpoint.rule.Identity`); otherwise `idn.findIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute(attr, "Equals", value, sortAttr)` (Equals/StartsWith only, max 50 results). Null-check the result and the email before using them, wrap in try/catch that logs with `log.debug/warn` (never log the email itself as sensitive data), and return a value on every path. Also consider whether a transform can do it instead: transforms are preferred over IdentityAttribute rules because they need no SailPoint review.
B: No. Cloud rules run in a restricted sandbox: direct use of context (SailPointContext) for getObjectByName, search, saveObject, commitTransaction etc. is rejected in review, as is querying the database directly. Use the provided helper instead: the idn object (IdnRuleUtil). Typical patterns: get the manager via identity.getManager() (if available on the passed-in Identity) and read its attribute with getStringAttribute("email") / getAttribute("email"), or use idn.getIdentityById(managerId) or idn.findIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute(...) to locate the identity. Better still, avoid the rule entirely: use a transform with the 'getReferenceIdentityAttribute' operation (uid "manager", attributeName "email") in the identity profile mapping. Remember IdentityAttribute rules must be null-safe (manager can be null during first aggregation) and fast, because they run on every identity refresh.

q: Which logging practices get an ISC rule rejected?
must: logging sensitive data (passwords, secrets, personal data) is prohibited and causes rejection
System.out/System.err and declaring your own logger are not allowed; use the provided log with debug/info/warn/error
log.error only for real errors; no full object serialization such as .toXml()
must_not: says System.out is fine because it goes to the VA log
A: Rejected (errors): `System.out.println` (not picked up by log aggregators; on the restriction list); declaring your own logger (`Logger.getLogger`, Log4j imports are restricted) - use the supplied `log`; logging sensitive data (passwords, personal data) - explicit rejection; logging full object serialization (`.toXml()` is prohibited; dumping whole identities/plans is flagged). Likely rejection/slower review (warnings): `log.error()` for informational messages - use `log.debug()` for debugging detail, `log.info()` for normal operation, `log.warn()` for non-critical issues, `log.error()` only for unexpected errors/critical failures; excessive or unnecessary logging calls (log sparingly but informatively). Also don't leave empty catch blocks: catch should log/handle. Note that for cloud rules (e.g. IdentityAttribute) logs are visible only to SailPoint personnel, so logging won't help you debug in production anyway.
B: Rejections typically come from: using System.out.println / printStackTrace (writes to stdout, not allowed); creating your own loggers with log4j directly or non-standard logger names; logging at info/debug level inside loops or for every identity (excessive volume on refresh/aggregation); logging sensitive data such as passwords, secrets, tokens, full account/identity attribute maps, PII (SSN, DOB), or the full ProvisioningPlan.toXml() which may contain password AttributeRequests; leaving debug statements that dump whole objects. Accepted practice: use the provided 'log' object (log.debug / log.info / log.warn / log.error), keep messages concise with a rule-name prefix, guard verbose ones with log.isDebugEnabled(), log errors in catch blocks with log.error rather than swallowing, and never log credentials. Connector-rule logs on the VA go to ccg.log, so be especially careful there.

q: I need to update an approved BeforeProvisioning rule but control exactly when the new logic goes live. How?
must: keep one rule per use case; versioned copies are not supported
submit '<original name>-TEMP', switch to it in the change window, validate, then update the original, switch back and ask to delete TEMP
need a specific window: tell SailPoint at least 48 hours in advance
must_not: recommends creating 'rule v2' and keeping both permanently
source: cloud-rules Review Guidelines (Updating Existing Rules and Versioning, Deployment Window); rules index SLAs
A: Use the `-TEMP` procedure from SailPoint's versioning guidelines (one rule per use case, versioned copies like `v2`/`new`/`copy` are not supported). 1) Submit the new logic as a separate rule named `<original name>-TEMP` (file `Rule - BeforeProvisioning - <name>-TEMP.xml`) and get it approved/deployed. 2) In your change window, switch the source's BeforeProvisioning rule reference to the TEMP rule and validate. 3) Submit the update of the original rule under the same name with the same logic. 4) Once deployed, switch the source back to the original. 5) Ask SailPoint to delete the TEMP rule. If you just need a timed deployment, tell SailPoint at least 48 hours ahead; for weekend go-lives deploy to sandbox first and promote to production yourself with sp-config export/import (`POST /sp-config/v1/export` / `/import`), which carries the approved signature without a new review. Remember BeforeProvisioning rules modify `plan` in place and return nothing.
B: Don't modify the live rule in place. Submit the new version as a separate rule with a new name (e.g., 'Before Provisioning - AD v2') via SailPoint review (or upload with the connector-rules API after validator if it's a connector rule). Once deployed, the new rule exists in the tenant but is not used by anything. When you're ready, switch the source to it by updating the source's beforeProvisioningRule reference (PATCH /v3/sources/{id}, path /beforeProvisioningRule with {type: RULE, id, name}). That swap is instant and reversible: rollback is just re-pointing to the old rule. Test first in a sandbox tenant on the same source config. After stabilization, request deletion of the old rule. Alternatively embed a feature flag in the rule reading a source attribute (e.g., from application.getAttributeValue("useNewLogic")) so you can toggle behavior through source config, but rule versioning plus re-pointing is the cleaner, auditable approach.

q: A colleague's AttributeGenerator rule calls idn.countIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute("email", "Contains", value) and loops over identity.getLinks(). Problems?
must: operation must be Equals or StartsWith (Contains is not supported) and the attribute must be searchable
iterating over accounts/identities (getLinks) is against the performance guidelines (cache bloat): use a targeted idn lookup
uniqueness checks are fine in AttributeGenerator rules (they are discouraged in IdentityAttribute rules)
source: idn_rule_utility; rules index Performance; identity_attribute_rule page
A: Several. 1) countIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute only supports operations like "Equals" (and StartsWith in some versions); "Contains" is not a valid/efficient operation and gives wrong uniqueness results, plus the attribute must be marked searchable. For uniqueness use "Equals" and also check accounts with idn.accountExistsByDisplayName / idn.attrSearchCountAccounts(sourceIds, "mail", "Equals", values) or isUniqueLDAPValue for AD/LDAP targets. 2) Looping over identity.getLinks() is expensive and frowned upon in review; with many accounts it hurts performance and links may not be loaded. Use idn.getFirstAccountByIdentityId or attribute-specific helpers (idn.getLinkAttribute...) instead. 3) Ensure the uniqueness loop has a max iteration bound (e.g., 100) and throws/returns an error rather than looping forever. 4) Normalize the value (lowercase, strip diacritics/spaces) before checking. Also consider whether a 'usernameGenerator' Create Profile config without a rule suffices.
B: Two errors. 1) `"Contains"` is not a supported operation: IdnRuleUtil searches accept only `"Equals"` or `"StartsWith"` (check R072; it throws otherwise). Signature is `int countIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute(String attributeName, String operation, String value)`, and the attribute must be a searchable identity attribute. For email uniqueness use `"Equals"`; for account values prefer `idn.attrSearchCountAccounts(List sourceIds, attr, "Equals", List values)` on a searchable account attribute, or `idn.isUniqueLDAPValue(identityNameOrId, applicationNameOrId, attr, value)` for AD/LDAP. 2) Looping over `identity.getLinks()` iterates over accounts (cache bloat; check R060) - replace with one targeted call such as `idn.getFirstAccountNativeIdentity(app, identityName)`, `idn.getAccountByNativeIdentity(app, id)` or `idn.getAccountAttribute(app, nativeId, attr)` (app = source name + ` [source]`). Also avoid idn lookups inside loops (R061); a bounded uniqueness retry loop (value, value1...) is the documented pattern but keep it short. Null-check returns and always return a value.
